doc: Mission 3, Mars Pathfinder (July 4, 1997): 'Land by bouncing' (issue #47). (1) The descent, in real time from the radar's first echo: the lander hangs on its 20 m bridle under the parachute and swings in the wind; the player steadies it, fires the three solid rockets at 98 m and cuts the bridle at 21.5 m, as the real sequence did (S-mpf-nssdc). Too fast at the ground and the airbags burst: lost, tried again. (2) The bounces: about 12 m up first, at least another 15 times, rolling to rest about 2.5 minutes and 1 km from the first impact (S-mpf-nssdc, S-mpf-nasa), shown faster (said on screen); the player steers the ball away from the big rocks while Inti counts. (3) The ramp: the airbags pulled in, the petals open, Sojourner rolls down the rear ramp, tilted 20 degrees (S-mpf-nasa), kept on it by the player; off the edge is lost. Climax: the first wheel on Mars, then NASA's pictures PIA00621 and PIA00633. Our simplifications, said on screen or here: the airbags' limit (26 m/s), the rockets' push (constant, about 2.2 s: enough to stop 70 m/s between 98 m and 21.5 m), slow motion near the two marks (said on screen), the wind, the rocks, Sojourner's speed on the ramp.

texts.steady: Steady the lander on its bridle: move the mouse left and right (or A/D) against the swing.
texts.fire: Press Space to fire the rockets
texts.cut: Press C to cut the bridle
texts.burst_sub: Too fast at the ground. That is not how it went: the real lander hit at 18 m/s and bounced. Try again.
texts.steer: Steer the ball away from the big rocks: mouse or A/D. Inti is counting.
texts.deflate: The airbags pull in. The petals open.
texts.drive: Drive Sojourner down the ramp: hold W (or the mouse button) to roll, mouse or A/D to stay in the middle.
texts.off_sub: That is not how it went: the real rover rolled down the rear ramp onto Mars. Try again.
texts.wheel_sub: The first wheeled vehicle on another planet.
texts.time_note: Real time while it falls. The bounces took about 2.5 minutes: shown 4 times faster.
texts.tangled: Still on the bridle at the ground.
texts.tangled_sub: That is not how it went: the bridle was cut 21.5 m up. Try again.

photos.caption: July 4, 1997: Sojourner still latched to its petal, the airbags pulled in, and Ares Vallis around it.
Sol 3: Sojourner's own camera sees its tracks in the Martian soil.

facts.text: The lander bounced about 12 meters into the air, then at least another 15 times, coming to rest about 2.5 minutes later and 1 km away.
Sojourner spent 83 days of a planned seven-day mission, the first wheeled vehicle on another planet.
